subtitle: Shaiva Stones, Jaina Copper: The Twin Paths of Kadamba Power

panels.shot: wide, slightly low-angle interior of a royal hall split visually: one side with a linga shrine, the other with a seated Jina image, the Kadamba Royal Patron between them
panels.action: Kadamba Royal Patron stands in the great hall of Banavasi, one hand resting near a Shaiva linga shrine, the other facing a serene Jina image, stone pillars rising around him in dim lamplight.

dialogue.text: In Banavasi, the Kadamba kings praised Shiva in stone and the Jina in copper, building a kingdom not of one faith, but of many.

i18n.hi: बनवासी में कदंब राजाओं ने पत्थर पर शिव, तांबे पर जिन की स्तुति कर बहु-धर्मी राज्य गढ़ा।

panels.shot: epic bird's-eye over Banavasi town with river, fields and temple spires, early morning mist
panels.action: From above, Banavasi spreads beside the river in soft dawn light, humble houses, rising plumes of smoke, and the dark silhouettes of early temples marking the skyline.

dialogue.text: In the fourth century, when the Kadambas rose in Banavasi, this forest town became a stage where old Vedic lines met new paths of faith.

i18n.hi: चौथी सदी में, जब कदंब बनवासी उठे, यह जंगल-बस्ती बनी जहाँ पुरानी वेद-रेखाएँ नई आस्थाओं से मिलीं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on the Talagunda pillar standing near a tank, with Kadamba Royal Patron in the middle ground, contemplative
panels.action: Near a broad, still tank, an inscribed stone pillar rises at Talagunda while Kadamba Royal Patron stands nearby, tracing the carved letters with a thoughtful gaze.

dialogue.text: At Talagunda, a stone pillar remembers their pride: Manavya-gotra Brahmanas, dharmamaharajas, guardians of tanks, temples and lineage.

i18n.hi: तलागुंडा का शिला-स्तंभ उनकी शान गाता है: मानव्य-गोत्र ब्राह्मण, धर्ममहाराज, तालाब, मंदिर और वंश के रक्षक।

panels.shot: medium close-up on Kadamba Royal Patron seated with Brahmana scribes, palm-leaf manuscripts in front, interior hall
panels.action: Kadamba Royal Patron sits cross-legged on a low platform as Brahmana scribes spread palm leaves before him, one pointing to a genealogy while oil lamps flicker.

dialogue.text: Their public face was clear: Brahmanical kings, rooted in gotra and dharma, shaping a landscape of shrines and tanks to mirror their order.

i18n.hi: खुली छवि साफ थी: गोत्र और धर्म में जड़े ब्राह्मण राजा, जो अपने अनुशासन जैसे मंदिर-तालाबों का भू-दृश्य रचते हैं।

panels.shot: low-angle wide shot of a Shaiva temple courtyard, with Kadamba Royal Patron overseeing artisans placing a linga
panels.action: In the courtyard of a Shaiva temple, Kadamba Royal Patron watches artisans lower a smooth linga onto its pedestal, priests stand nearby, and villagers gather in respectful distance.

dialogue.text: Madhukeshvara, Praneshvara: names of Shiva that clung to Kadamba stones, as shrines rose and bells folded the land into Shaiva sound.

i18n.hi: मधुकेश्वर, प्राणेश्वर—शिव के ये नाम कदंब शिलाओं से चिपक गए, जब मंदिर उठे और घंटियाँ भूमि को शैव ध्वनि में बाँध गईं।

panels.shot: tight close-up on a copper plate charter being unrolled by the king’s hand, engraved letters catching the light
panels.action: Kadamba Royal Patron’s hand gently unrolls a fresh set of copper plates, the engraved letters gleaming as a scribe looks on, waiting for his reaction.

dialogue.text: Yet at Halasi, the same court unrolled copper that began not with Shiva, but with a different praise: Jayati Bhagavan Jinendra.

i18n.hi: पर हलसी में, उसी दरबार ने तांबे पर लेख खोला, शिव से नहीं, एक और स्तुति से: जयति भगवान जिनेंद्र।

panels.shot: medium shot of Kadamba Royal Patron listening to a Jain acharya in a simple mandapa, contrast with royal ornaments
panels.action: Inside a plain pillared mandapa at Halasi, a serene Jain monk sits on a low seat, while Kadamba Royal Patron, richly adorned, listens intently with folded hands.

dialogue.speaker: kadamba_patrons
dialogue.text: Your path is gentle, acharya. Our land must learn to hold many paths.

i18n.hi: तुम्हारा मार्ग कोमल है, आचार्य। हमारी भूमि को अनेक रास्ते सँभालना सीखना होगा।

panels.shot: wide shot of a donation ceremony at Halasi: king granting land, Jain monks and officials present
panels.action: In an open courtyard near Halasi, Kadamba Royal Patron offers a ceremonial pot of earth to a group of Jain monks, while officials with writing boards stand ready to record the grant.

dialogue.text: Kakusthavarma’s plates speak of Jina first, then of land and rights, marking Halasi as a place where Jain teachers found royal shelter.

i18n.hi: ककुष्ठवर्मा की ताम्रपट्टियाँ पहले जिन, फिर भूमि और अधिकार कहती हैं, हलसी को जैन आचार्यों की शरण में दरबार दिखाती हैं।

panels.shot: split-depth shot: foreground Jain monks teaching, background Shaiva priests at a temple, both within the same townscape
panels.action: Within the same town, Jain monks teach under a tree in the foreground while, in the background, Shaiva priests tend to a temple courtyard, both scenes unfolding under the same sky.

dialogue.text: Palasika, Halasi, Banavasi: the records show Jina shrines near Shiva temples, Jain acharyas and Shaiva priests walking the same dusty streets.

i18n.hi: पालसिका, हलसी, बनवासी—शिलालेखों में शिव मंदिरों के पास जिन देवालय, उन्हीं गलियों में जैन आचार्य और शैव पुजारी चलते दिखते हैं।

panels.shot: interior court scene, slightly high angle, showing multiple groups: Brahmana ritualists, Jain monks, royal counselors
panels.action: In the royal court, Kadamba Royal Patron sits on the throne while to one side Brahmana ritualists present a Vedic text, and to the other Jain monks stand calmly, as counselors murmur between them.

dialogue.text: Some scholars call them Shaiva, some Jain, some simply Brahmanical kings. The inscriptions refuse a simple story of one conversion and one creed.

i18n.hi: कुछ विद्वान उन्हें शैव, कुछ जैन, कुछ सिर्फ ब्राह्मण राजा कहते हैं; शिलालेख एक सीधी दीक्षा और एक मत की कहानी नहीं मानते।

panels.shot: medium close-up on the king in quiet debate with two advisors representing different traditions, candlelight casting long shadows
panels.action: By lamplight, Kadamba Royal Patron leans forward as two advisors, one with sacred thread and one with a Jain monk’s robe, speak in turn, their shadows tall upon the wall.

dialogue.speaker: kadamba_patrons
dialogue.text: Our duty is rajadharma. Let it not be narrowed by one banner.

i18n.hi: हमारा धर्म है राजधर्म, उसे एक ही ध्वज में कैद मत करो।

panels.shot: dynamic oblique view of scribes engraving different invocations on separate plates, piles of copper sheets around
panels.action: In the royal records office, scribes sit cross-legged engraving invocations onto copper plates, some beginning with Shaiva praises, others with the Jina, stacked neatly beside them.

dialogue.text: One grant to a Shaiva temple, another to a Jain sangha: the Kadamba chancery learned to switch invocations as easily as it moved from forest to field.

i18n.hi: एक दान शैव मंदिर को, दूसरा जैन संघ को—कदंब दफ्तर ने उतनी ही सहजता से आरंभ बदले, जितनी से जंगल से खेत तक बढ़े।

panels.shot: wide dusk shot of Banavasi with both temple shikharas and simple Jain basadi roofs visible, smoke rising
panels.action: At dusk, Banavasi’s skyline shows the outlines of temple towers and the plainer roofs of Jain basadis, while cook fires send smoke curling over the clustered houses.

dialogue.text: From c. 345 to 540, under Kadamba rule, the town’s sacred map thickened: Shaiva spires, Jain halls, ponds that served all.

i18n.hi: लगभग ३४५ से ५४० तक कदंब शासन में नगर का पवित्र नक्शा घना हुआ—शैव शिखर, जैन सभा-भवन, सबके तालाब।

panels.shot: subtle low-angle on Kadamba Royal Patron walking along a temple tank embankment, reflecting in the water with both shrines in the background
panels.action: Kadamba Royal Patron walks slowly along a stone embankment of a temple tank, his reflection wavering in the water that also mirrors a Shiva temple and a Jain hall behind him.

dialogue.text: Their pillar at Talagunda remembers a tank beside a temple, but their copper from Halasi remembers Jina first; together they hint at a policy of layered patronage.

i18n.hi: तलागुंडा का स्तंभ मंदिर-तालाब की जोड़ी याद रखता है, हलसी का तांबा जिन को पहले बुलाता है; दोनों मिलकर परतदार संरक्षण नीति का इशारा देते हैं।

panels.shot: intercut-style composition: ghosted overlays of later dynasties and Xuanzang’s imagined visit, with Kadamba king as a faint earlier layer
panels.action: Against a faded backdrop of Kadamba Royal Patron, faint images of later kings and a distant monk-traveller appear like translucent layers, hinting at centuries of change in Banavasi.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, Xuanzang saw Buddhist Banavasi, but his report belongs to another age; the Kadambas’ record is Shaiva-Jain, not a hidden Buddhist kingdom.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद हुएंशांग ने बौद्ध बनवासी देखा, पर वो दूसरी उम्र की कथा है; कदंबों का लेखा शैव–जैन है, कोई छिपा बौद्ध राज्य नहीं।

panels.shot: close-up on weathered hands of a modern researcher holding rubbings of inscriptions, overlays of ancient script visible
panels.action: A modern scholar’s hands hold ink rubbings of Kadamba inscriptions, the ancient scripts dark against white paper, as though the voices of Talagunda and Halasi speak again.

dialogue.text: Today, historians read their pillars and plates and find no single faith-flag to raise, only a pattern of support that shifted with place, purpose and audience.

i18n.hi: आज इतिहासकार उनकी शिलाएँ और ताम्रपट पढ़ते हैं और एक भी धर्म-ध्वज नहीं पाते, बस स्थान, उद्देश्य और श्रोताओं संग बदलता संरक्षण पैटर्न।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot: ruins and standing temples at Banavasi and Halasi under a vast sky, tiny human figures walking between
panels.action: Under a wide, pale sky, surviving temples at Banavasi and Halasi stand among ruins, small figures walking quietly between a Shiva shrine and a Jain basadi that share the same ground.

dialogue.text: Between Shiva and the Jina, the Kadambas learned that a kingdom can endure not by one sacred path alone, but by holding many in its shadow.

i18n.hi: शिव और जिन के बीच कदंबों ने सीखा कि राज्य टिकता है एक ही पथ से नहीं, कई पवित्र राहों को अपनी छाया में रखकर।

subtitle_i18n.en: Shaiva Stones, Jaina Copper: The Twin Paths of Kadamba Power
subtitle_i18n.hi: शैव पत्थर, जैन तांबा: कदंब शक्ति के दो रास्ते
